q: President poll announced. Who correctly forms electoral college?
options: Elected MPs plus elected MLAs only
All MPs plus nominated members and MLCs
expl: Elected MPs+MLAs incl Delhi/Puducherry vote; nominated, MLCs excluded.
why: Nominated members do not vote for President. MLCs have no role. Weight follows population.

q: Bill passed by Houses sent for approval. President can?
expl: Suspensive veto only once; if repassed must assent; no return for Money.
why: Single return checks delay. Second passage makes assent mandatory, preserving parliamentary supremacy.

q: Parliament not in session, urgent law needed. President issues temporary law. Life?
options: Dies 6 weeks after reassembly unless passed
expl: Ordinance must be laid; lapses 6 weeks after reassembly if not approved.
why: Ordinance is stopgap, not parallel legislation. House approval decides survival.

q: Death convict seeks mercy. President power and limit?
options: Pardon with limited court review for mala fide
expl: Art 72 pardon reviewable per Epuru Sudhakar for mala fide, irrelevance.
why: Mercy is not personal charity. Courts check abuse while respecting clemency wisdom.

q: VP chairing RS, President post vacant. Correct?
options: VP acts max 6 months till poll
expl: VP acts as President during vacancy; election within 6 months.
why: Vacancy is temporary bridge. Fresh election fills office, VP returns to RS role.

q: Governor gets state Bill. Lawful options?
options: Assent, withhold, return once, or reserve for President
expl: Art 200 gives four choices; Money Bill cannot be returned.
why: Governor is legislative link, not maker. Reservation brings Union scrutiny where needed.

q: State House adjourned, urgent ordinance needed. Governor acts. Validity?
expl: Art 213 ordinance lapses 6 weeks after reassembly if not passed.
why: Same stopgap logic as Union. Repromulgation without House is fraud per Wadhwa.

q: Council of Ministers size after 2003 reform. Correct?
expl: 91st caps ministers at 15% with floor of 12.
why: Cap curbs jumbo cabinets. Both Union and States bound, relevant to AP assembly math.

q: Disqualified defector wants minister post immediately. Position?
expl: 91st bars defector-disqualified from minister till fresh election.
why: Bar links anti-defection to executive purity. Re-election cleanses disqualification.

q: Bihar-style repeated ordinances without House. Court view?
expl: D.C. Wadhwa condemned repromulgation bypassing legislature.
why: Ordinance is emergency legislation. Bypassing House subverts legislative supremacy.

q: Compare electors: President vs VP. Correct?
expl: President includes MLAs, excludes nominated; VP MPs incl nominated, no MLAs.
why: Design balances federal vs parliamentary roles. Mixing colleges is common trap.

q: Compare veto: ordinary vs Money Bill at Union. Correct?
options: Ordinary returnable once; Money not returnable
expl: Suspensive veto once for ordinary; no return for Money Bills.
why: Money reflects LS supremacy with Speaker certification. Delaying it via return is barred.

q: Compare pardon: President vs Governor. Correct?
options: President covers death, court-martial, Union law; Governor narrower state law
expl: President wider; Governor limited to state law, no court-martial/death full scope.
why: Hierarchy reserves military and death finality to President. Governor acts within state list.

q: Compare ordinance: Union vs State. Correct?
options: Both need House gap, urgency, six-week lapse
expl: Both are gap-urgency stopgaps lapsing 6 weeks after reassembly.
why: Logic is parallel across levels. Authority differs but temporal control is same.

q: Compare removal: President vs VP. Correct?
options: President impeachment violation charge; VP RS resolution plus LS agree
expl: President needs 1/4th notice 2/3rd; VP needs RS majority LS concurrence 14 days.
why: Higher bar for President reflects stature. VP process is political resolution, not impeachment.

q: Statements: 1 Nominated MPs vote President. 2 MLAs vote President. 3 MLCs vote President. Correct?
expl: Only elected MPs+MLAs vote; nominated and MLCs excluded.
why: Statements 1 and 3 add ineligible voters. Only elected legislators form college.

q: Statements: 1 Veto can be used endlessly. 2 If repassed must assent. 3 Money returnable. Correct?
expl: Return only once; repass binds; Money not returnable.
why: Statements 1 and 3 claim extra returns. Constitution allows single suspensive return only.

q: Statements: 1 Ordinance permanent. 2 Lays before House. 3 Dies 6 weeks after reassembly. Correct?
expl: Temporary, must be laid, lapses in 6 weeks if not passed.
why: Statement 1 claims permanence. Laying and lapse prove stopgap nature.

q: Statements: 1 Pardon unreviewable. 2 Wadhwa allows repromulgation. 3 Defector bar till re-elected. Correct?
expl: Pardon reviewable Sudhakar; Wadhwa condemns; defector bar true.
why: Statements 1 and 2 invert case law. Only 91st bar statement survives scrutiny.

q: Statements: 1 VP elector includes MLAs. 2 VP acts max 6 months. 3 Ministers max 15%. Correct?
expl: VP by MPs only; 6-month acting; 15% cap true.
why: Statement 1 adds MLAs wrongly. Acting cap and minister cap are settled numeric limits.
